claims.text: What the image looks like Hepatic hypodensity with rim enhancement → pyogenic abscess vs metastasis
claims.quote: Hepatic hypodensity with rim enhancement Pyogenic abscess vs metastasis

claims.text: Example MRI of metastatic liver cancer: areas of low attenuation inside the liver, an appearance typical of metastases
claims.quote: An abnormal MRI of the chest shows areas of low attenuation (marked with arrows) inside the liver. This appearance is typical of metastatic liver cancer.

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Amebiasis: often without obvious dysentery; usually a large single abscess with liquefaction; systemic illness, tender hepatomegaly, surprisingly mild liver dysfunction
claims.quote: Amebiasis§ | Important disease, often without obvious dysentery Usually a large single abscess with liquefaction Systemic illness, tender hepatomegaly, surprisingly mild liver dysfunction

claims.text: Metastases are suspected with weight loss and hepatomegaly or a primary tumor likely to spread to the liver
claims.quote: Liver metastases are suspected in patients with weight loss and hepatomegaly or with primary tumors likely to spread to the liver.

claims.text: Labs are usually not specific: alkaline phosphatase, GGT and sometimes LDH typically rise earlier or more than other tests; aminotransferases vary
claims.quote: If metastases are suspected, laboratory tests are often performed, but results are usually not specific for the diagnosis. Alkaline phosphatase, gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase, and sometimes lactate dehydrogenase typically increase earlier or to a greater degree than do other test results; aminotransferase levels vary.

claims.text: Imaging has good sensitivity and specificity: ultrasound is usually helpful, but CT or MRI with contrast is often more accurate
claims.quote: Imaging tests have good sensitivity and specificity. Ultrasound is usually helpful, but CT with contrast or MRI with contrast is often more accurate.

claims.text: Image-guided liver biopsy gives the definitive diagnosis; done if other tests are equivocal or histology (eg, cell type) may guide treatment
claims.quote: Liver biopsy guided by imaging provides the definitive diagnosis and is performed if other tests are equivocal or if histologic information (eg, cell type of the liver metastasis) may help determine the treatment plan.

claims.text: Causes Pyogenic abscess: serious infection acquired via portal pyemia, cholangitis, or hematogenous or direct spread; various organisms, especially gram-negative and anaerobic
claims.quote: Pyogenic abscess § | Serious infection acquired via portal pyemia, cholangitis, or hematogenous or direct spread; due to various organisms, especially gram-negative and anaerobic

claims.text: Metastases: more common than primary liver cancer and sometimes the first manifestation of a cancer of the GI tract, breast, lung or pancreas
claims.quote: Metastatic liver cancer is more common than primary liver cancer and is sometimes the initial clinical manifestation of cancer originating in the gastrointestinal tract, breast, lung, or pancreas.

claims.text: Symptoms Pyogenic abscess: illness and toxicity, yet only mild liver dysfunction
claims.quote: Illness and toxicity, yet only mild liver dysfunction
claims.locator: Selected Infections With Liver Involvement table

claims.text: Metastases: early ones may be asymptomatic; nonspecific symptoms (eg, weight loss, anorexia, fever) often come first; the liver may be enlarged, hard or tender; massive hepatomegaly with easily palpable nodules signifies advanced disease
claims.quote: Early liver metastases may be asymptomatic. Nonspecific symptoms of cancer (eg, weight loss, anorexia, fever) often develop first. The liver may be enlarged, hard, or tender; massive hepatomegaly with easily palpable nodules signifies advanced disease.

claims.text: Peritoneal tumor seeding may produce ascites; jaundice is usually absent or mild initially unless a tumor obstructs the bile ducts
claims.quote: Concomitant peritoneal tumor seeding may produce ascites, but jaundice is usually absent or mild initially unless a tumor causes biliary obstruction.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: drain abscess; oncology workup if mets
claims.quote: Drain abscess; oncology workup if mets

claims.text: Metastases: treatment depends on the extent; with solitary or very few colorectal metastases, surgical resection may prolong survival; systemic chemotherapy may shrink tumors and prolong life but is not curative
claims.quote: Treatment depends on the extent of metastasis. With solitary or very few metastases due to colorectal cancer, surgical resection may prolong survival. Depending on characteristics of the primary tumor, systemic chemotherapy may shrink tumors and prolong life but is not curative; hepatic intra-arterial chemotherapy sometimes has the same effect but with fewer or milder systemic adverse effects.

claims.text: Liver radiation occasionally relieves severe pain from advanced metastases but does not prolong life; extensive disease is fatal and is best managed by palliation and family support
claims.quote: Radiation therapy to the liver occasionally alleviates severe pain due to advanced metastases but does not prolong life. Extensive disease is fatal and is best managed by palliation for the patient and support for the family (see The Dying Patient).
